subject: Data handling follow-up: data retention exception & PII requirements
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Matt Jensen <matt.jensen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Data handling follow-up: data retention exception & PII requirements

Hi Matt — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we're all aligned: \

Call recap:\
- Main ask: Acme Health needs assurance that PII from clinical notes will not be retained by the inference service (0-retention) and that logs containing any identifiers are either not stored or retained under a very short schedule.
- Data residency: Primary requirement is US-only processing & logging.
- Compliance: You asked for evidence (SOC 2, data flow diagrams) and sample contract language for a data retention exception.

What Redwood can offer (high level):
- Ephemeral inference mode / 0-retention: conversational payloads are not written to persistent storage by default; KV caches are in-memory only and cleared per-session when configured.
- Shortened audit/log retention: we can limit service-level audit logs (errors/trace) to a short window (configurable) and provide a tailored retention schedule as an exception.
- Private/Dedicated options: Dedicated capacity or Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) if you require stricter isolation.
- Technical mitigations: client-side hashing/redaction for identifiers and custom tokenization hooks.

Attachments: redwood-data-handling-summary.pdf — high-level options and implementation notes.

Proposed next steps:\
1) I can loop in our Security & Compliance lead (Marissa) and CS (Rafael) to draft a tailored retention amendment.
2) If you confirm 0-retention for conversational content is required (and short retention for audit logs), we'll prepare a formal Data Retention Exception request and proposed contract wording.
3) Share any legal/technical contacts to include on the thread so we can move to redlines.

Do you want us to propose language this week? Happy to schedule a quick follow-up with Marissa if useful.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Matt Jensen <matt.jensen@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Data handling follow-up: data retention exception & PII requirements

Camila — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: \

- Confirmed: Acme requires 0-retention of PII-containing conversational content. We cannot allow the raw PII to be stored in persistent logs.
- Audit logs: We are OK with a very short retention window (<=7 days) for operational logs, but any audit/event data that could be tied to patient identifiers must be redacted or avoided.
- Residency: We must keep processing and logs within US regions. EU is not acceptable for this workload.
- Evidence: We need a sample contract amendment, a short description of the technical controls, and any current SOC 2 report indicators you can share.

Looping in procurement: procurement@acmehealth.com for timing and next steps. Procurement will expect a proposed amendment and note on billing impact if this requires dedicated capacity.

Can Marissa provide the technical assurance language? We can target an answer on contract redlines by EOD next week if you provide the proposed text.

Regards,
Matt Jensen
Director, Digital Health
Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Data handling follow-up: data retention exception & PII requirements

Hi Matt / team — thanks for the details. Below is the technical assurance language and options from Redwood Security & Compliance. I'm pasting the suggested clause and a short implementation note.

Suggested contract clause (draft):
"Redwood agrees to configure Customer's inference workloads in Ephemeral Mode such that conversational request and response payloads are not written to persistent storage. System operational logs that do not contain direct patient identifiers may be retained for a maximum period of 7 days. Redwood will provide Customer with redacted audit exports upon request for legitimate audit purposes. Any deviation from these retention parameters will require a mutually executed Data Retention Exception signed by authorized representatives of both parties."

Implementation notes:
- 0-retention: We support Ephemeral Mode on hosted and dedicated backends. For hosted deployments, we disable persistent conversational logging and ensure KV caches are cleared at session end.
- Audit/operational logs: By default we record minimal telemetry for stability; for Acme we propose enabling redaction and limiting retention to 7 days. We can provide a trimmed audit export (redacted) on request.
- Data residency: We will pin Acme's workload to US regions only and confirm physical host region controls as part of the security package.
- Mitigations: Recommend client-side hashing/tokenization for patient identifiers and avoid sending direct PHI where possible.

Impacts & timeline:
- Hosted Ephemeral Mode: minimal implementation time (1-2 weeks for config + verification).
- Dedicated/Private: ~4-8 weeks depending on procurement and infra. Dedicated will have additional monthly cost.
- Legal/contract: we'll provide a proposed amendment and example redline for your counsel.

Attachments I uploaded for evidence: security-evidence.zip (SOC 2 summary, architecture diagram, data flow).

I'll work with Camila to produce the amendment text for legal. Rafael — can you confirm if CS will need any onboarding resources for Dedicated vs Hosted changes?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
